messages:
anya_ml: Quick heads-up — I hit a perf regression in the autotuner for FlashAttention/SDPA on ff4 when head_dim=48. Profiling below.

devon: Can you paste the numbers? :eyes:

anya_ml:
```
baseline (no FA): 12.3 ms/token
FA v1 (non-causal): 8.2 ms/token
FA v2 (causal): 9.1 ms/token
FA v3 (autotuned): 13.8 ms/token  <-- regression (head_dim=48)
config: seq_len=1024, batch=4, kv_cache enabled, sm90 hosts
```

maria_s: That smells like head-dim alignment. 48 isn't a nice multiple of 32/64 so some kernels take a slow fallback path. Is the autotuner selecting SDPA-v3 for causal workloads by mistake?

kev: I saw a similar pattern last month. Our selection rule currently goes by seq_len thresholds (v3 for >512) but ignores (causal vs non-causal) and head_dim % 16/32 constraints. For certain head dims v3 falls back to a scalar path.

anya_ml: Repro script: 
```
python perf_test.py --model ff4 --head-dim 48 --seq-len 1024 --batch 4 --kv-cache --flashattn
```

devon: Logs show kernel name resolved as `sdpa_v3_causal_small_heads` but the compiled kernel contains a fallback that performs much worse when head_dim%16 != 0. So autotuner's cost model is inaccurate for these edge head sizes.

kev: Proposed quick fix: update kernel-selection rules in the autotuner to be architecture-aware and consider both `causal` flag and `head_dim` alignment. Pseudocode: 
```
if causal:
  if head_dim % 32 != 0: prefer sdpa_v1_or_v2
  elif seq_len <= 512: prefer sdpa_v2
  else: prefer sdpa_v3
else:
  follow existing non-causal heuristics
```
Also distinguish sm70 vs sm90 because sm90 has better vectorization for v3.

maria_s: Also remember KV cache: effective seq_len = kv_cache_len + request_seq_len. Autotuner must include kv cache in decision. Right now we only look at request seq length which underestimates real working size.

anya_ml: Agreed. I'll add two changes: (1) incorporate `kv_cache_len` into seq_len heuristics; (2) add head_dim alignment checks to avoid scalar fallbacks. I'll run staging canary.

devon: Add a unit test matrix to avoid regressions. Minimal matrix: 
- head_dim in {32,48,64,80}
- seq_len in {128,512,1024}
- causal {true,false}
- kv_cache_len {0,512}
Make perf assertions on p50/p95 vs baseline.

maria_s: Also add counters to the runtime so we can monitor which kernel variant was chosen on prod traffic (metric: `kernelselection.flashattn.v{1,2,3}.count`).

ops-bot: deploy: canary started for runtime/autotune head-dim fix -> hosts: rrt-ml-14, rrt-ml-21 :rocket:

anya_ml: Opening PR with tests and selection rules. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3245  (branch: fix/autotune-head-dim-48, commit c3f9a2b)

kev: Nice. Also add a short flamegraph link for the failing case so infra folks can eyeball memory/warp stalls: https://perf.redwood.ai/graphs/ff4-head48-v3-2026-02-07 :eyes:

devon: Once PR is in, run hammer test (100k requests, mixed sizes, KV on) and compare p50/p95. If green we roll to prod end of week.

anya_ml: Will run A/B in staging tomorrow morning and post results here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
